To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD1 molecules are not transported from MIIC to the surface during DC maturation, but DC maturation-independent CD1-mediated presentation of lipid Ags is highly effective.

CD1 molecules are not trafficked to the plasma membrane in the manner of MHC class I and class II molecules during dendritic cell (DC) maturation and that DCs efficiently present Ags via CD1 molecules to lipid Ag-specific T cells before they are fully matured.
DC maturation does not alter CD1 trafficking, CD1 Ag loading, or CD1-restricted Ag presentation, in contrast to MHC class II.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which dendritic cells ( DCs) present Ag to T cells and with the consequences of DC maturation on Ag presentation.
how the innate and adaptive immune systems communicate with each other.

the mechanisms that regulate the intracellular trafficking of MHC class I and MHC class II in dendritic cells (1, 2) and the consequences of this trafficking for the presentation of peptide and lipid Ags to T lymphocytes (2, 3).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD1 molecules are not efficiently transported to the cell surface upon maturation and, as a consequence, are less likely to be presented on the surface of mature DCs than MHC molecules.
the CD1 molecules are not regulated by DC maturation in the same fashion as MHC class II and, as a result, are not involved in the regulation of the Ag presentation capacity of DCs.
CD1 molecules traffic and present Ag independently of MHC molecules in human DCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presentation of lipid Ags by CD1 molecules on the surface of DCs is not regulated by the same mechanisms that govern the presentation of peptide Ags on MHC class II.
DC maturation does not significantly affect CD1 trafficking, but it may have a profound impact upon CD1 Ag presentation to T cells.
the presentation of lipid Ags by CD1 molecules is not affected by DC maturation, which may be important for early Ag presentation by DCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DC maturation does not significantly affect the trafficking of CD1 molecules.
